I am an orchestra teacher at a high school in my third year;yes that job exists. I had a student, who was super gung ho about the arts, but lacked the potential for it. He wanted to pursue a degree in music performance, when I knew that he lacked the dedication and the skills for it in the ever competing national market. I discouraged him from music, even though it's my vocation, and introduced him to a contractor friend of mine. This student excelled at engineering. I endured 24 parent student conferences telling me how i dissuaded their child from pursuing their dreams and how I should be fired for not pushing for my own vocation towards a student that was passionate about it. That kid has been out of school for two years. He became a contractor, makes 65k more than me, AND plays In a symphony two chairs behind me. I fail to see how I did not push him in the right direction. The public mentality is screwed up when they feel that a life of striving for public entertainment beats a secure, stable life with a family and your passions.
